protocol.instrument_name: NSW Pharmacist Practice Standards for Management of Mild, Acute Musculoskeletal Pain
protocol.instrument_version: NSW Health Authority (dated 25 February 2026); approved 25 February 2026
protocol.legal_basis: Not stated as a named regulation or poisons schedule provision. The document states 'Approved Medicines as listed in the NSW Health Authority (dated 25 February 2026)', that supply occurs 'under the Authority', that pharmacists must have 'successfully completed all training requirements detailed in the NSW Health Authority (dated 25 February 2026)', and it is approved by 'Dr Kerry Chant AO PSM, Chief Health Officer and Deputy Secretary, Population and Public Health, 25 February 2026'. Basis for the standard is the Queensland Community Pharmacy Scope of Practice Pilot Mild, Acute Musculoskeletal Pain - Clinical Practice Guideline (2024) plus NSW Health ECAT protocols.
protocol.supervision_model: 'approved pharmacist' / 'participating approved pharmacist' model: 'Pharmacists must hold general registration under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law and have successfully completed all training requirements detailed in the NSW Health Authority (dated 25 February 2026).' 'Pharmacists must exercise professional discretion and judgement when applying the information contained within this Practice Standard, The Practice Standard does not override the responsibility of the pharmacist to make decisions appropriate to the circumstances of the individual, in consultation with the patient and/or their carer.' Community Pharmacy Mild, Acute Musculoskeletal Pain Service.
protocol.scope_summary: Practice standard for the Community Pharmacy Mild, Acute Musculoskeletal Pain Service (NSW): appropriately trained approved pharmacists assess and manage patients aged >=18 years with mild, acute (acute mechanical, self-limiting <3 months) musculoskeletal pain, provided no red flag or referral criterion is met, with informed clinical and financial consent, patient history/clinical review/examination, a management plan of non-pharmacological measures plus Section A Approved Medicines (oral formulations of celecoxib, etoricoxib, indometacin, ketoprofen, meloxicam, naproxen IR, naproxen MR, piroxicam, diclofenac), counselling, documentation (electronic clinical record, dispensing record, My Health Record upload, records stored securely minimum seven (7) years) and referral rules. Opioids cannot be prescribed under the Authority for this service; clinical review with the pharmacist is generally not required.

diagnosis_pathways.name: Patient assessment flowchart and management pathway for mild, acute musculoskeletal pain (Section D flowchart, Sections I-J assessment and management)

steps.description: Flowchart entry: 'Patient presents to a participating approved pharmacist for management of mild acute musculoskeletal pain'. Age gate: 'Is the patient >=18 years old?' - No branch: 'Not eligible for management under the Authority and Practice Standard. Refer to GP.'

Red flag / exclusion gate: 'Does the patient have any acute respiratory signs, red flags, or exclusions?' (verbatim; see open_questions) - Yes branch: 'Not eligible for management under the Authority and Practice Standard. Refer to Emergency Department or GP.'

gates.criterion: No acute signs, red flags or exclusions (none of the Section G red flags or referral criteria met)

steps.description: Conduct patient informed consent: '• Participation • Financial • Pharmacist communication with other health practitioners' - No branch: 'Not eligible for management under the Authority and Practice Standard. Refer to GP.' 'Informed clinical and financial consent should be obtained from the patient prior to providing the service.'

gates.criterion: Informed consent obtained for participation, financial consent, and pharmacist communication with other health practitioners

steps.description: Flowchart: 'Conduct patient history and clinical review including review of contraindications, precautions, drug interactions, pregnancy and lactation status'.

gates.criterion: Patient history and clinical review completed including contraindications, precautions, drug interactions, pregnancy and lactation status

steps.description: PATIENT HISTORY: 'A patient history, pain history and assessment and an examination that is tailored to the patient's presentation is required to inform the management approach, including appropriate referral.' History should include age; pregnancy and lactation status; presenting complaint; mechanism of injury; preceding events (e.g. syncope, chest pain or dizziness); non-musculoskeletal symptoms that may indicate serious pathology (weight loss or gain, fever, malaise, new rash, nausea, vomiting, sweating); alerting symptoms and features as per Therapeutic Guidelines; medical history (rheumatological/autoimmune conditions, cancer, osteoporosis, immunosuppression, ischaemic heart disease, renal disease); surgical history; family history; risk factors for acute rheumatic fever; response to previous treatments; impacts on quality of life; current/recently commenced/ceased medicines; weight, diet, exercise; allergies/adverse drug reactions; alcohol, tobacco and other drug history; other psychosocial factors. 'For patients aged over 50 years, consider the increased risk of serious underlying pathologies such as malignancy and minimal-trauma fractures.' The My Health Record should be reviewed where appropriate and available.

gates.criterion: Sufficient information obtained to assess whether the presentation is consistent with mild, acute MSK pain, whether any referral criterion is met, and the safety and appropriateness of any medicines supplied

steps.description: PAIN HISTORY AND ASSESSMENT: 'Pain history and assessment should be conducted in accordance with the Therapeutic Guidelines: Assessing a patient with pain and General principles of acute pain management.' Pain severity is subjective and interpreted in context. 'If the patient's self-reported pain severity is not consistent with other assessment findings e.g. physical function or examination findings, the patient should be referred to a medical practitioner for comprehensive assessment including socio-psycho-biomedical factors.'

gates.criterion: Self-reported pain severity consistent with other assessment findings (physical function, examination findings)

steps.description: EXAMINATION: 'Where appropriate, conduct an assessment of vital signs.' Examine the area of pain in accordance with Therapeutic Guidelines: Clinical assessment of musculoskeletal symptoms in adults and (if applicable) Assessment of back and neck pain; refer to NSW Health acute lower back pain assessment and musculoskeletal assessment for additional guidance. 'To determine appropriate management or referral, it is important to identify the aetiology of the pain (nociceptive, neuropathic, nociplastic, or combination (mixed pain)) and to distinguish pain associated with inflammation from mechanical pain (Table 1).' MSK pain is predominantly nociceptive; acute pain is defined by duration of less than 3 months. Table 1 (clinical features of mechanical versus inflammatory pain): inflammatory - improves with exercise/movement, does not improve with rest, lasts more than 3 months, morning stiffness >30 minutes, pain waking during second half of the night with improvement on getting up; mechanical - may worsen with movement/exercise, often improves with rest, most cases acute onset lasting less than 3 months, precipitating physical injury may be identifiable.

gates.criterion: Aetiology of pain identified (nociceptive, neuropathic, nociplastic, or mixed) and inflammatory pain distinguished from mechanical pain

steps.description: Investigations: 'Referral to a medical practitioner for management, including investigations, may be required for acute pain that does not respond to management, or if indicated by patient history and/or pain history e.g. patients presenting with traumatic injuries that may require radiological examination.'

gates.criterion: Acute pain responds to management, or history/pain history does not indicate need for investigations (e.g. radiological examination after traumatic injury)

steps.description: CONFIRM MANAGEMENT IS APPROPRIATE: 'Pharmacists must consult the Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook and other relevant references to confirm the management is appropriate, including for: • Contraindications and precautions • Drug interactions • Pregnancy and lactation.' NB1: 'NSAID selection should be based on patient factors, including contraindications, and balance the risks and benefits. Refer to Therapeutic Guidelines: Principles of NSAID use for musculoskeletal pain for guidance.'

gates.criterion: Contraindications, precautions, drug interactions and pregnancy/lactation checked against Therapeutic Guidelines/AMH and no contraindication to the planned management

steps.description: Establish management plan. 'Pharmacist management of mild, acute MSK pain involves: • Non-pharmacological and lifestyle measures: advice regarding non-pharmacological pain management strategies for all patients in accordance with the Therapeutic Guidelines: Non-pharmacological management of acute pain • Pharmacotherapy: in accordance with the Therapeutic Guidelines: Pharmacological management of acute pain, Principles of NSAID use for musculoskeletal pain and Principles of paracetamol use for musculoskeletal pain.' Approved Medicines (Section A, oral formulations): celecoxib, etoricoxib, indometacin, ketoprofen, meloxicam, naproxen immediate-release, naproxen modified-release, piroxicam, diclofenac. 'Non-pharmacological therapies and lifestyle measures ... and pharmacotherapy (paracetamol and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)) should be considered in the overall management plan for mild, acute MSK pain.' 'Opioids are not required for the management of mild MSK pain and cannot be prescribed under the Authority for this service.' Site-specific advice per Therapeutic Guidelines: Overview of limb conditions, Nonspecific low back pain, Nonspecific neck pain, Nonspecific thoracic pain.

gates.criterion: Patient meets all inclusion criteria and no referral criterion/red flag is met
Only formulations listed in Section A Approved Medicines supplied (opioids cannot be supplied)
Dose, frequency and duration per Therapeutic Guidelines confirmed for the individual patient

steps.description: COMMUNICATE AGREED MANAGEMENT PLAN: 'Comprehensive advice and counselling (including supporting written information when required) as per the Therapeutic Guidelines, Australian Medicines Handbook and other relevant references should be provided to the patient regarding: • The possible diagnosis, management options and expectations for resolution • Product and medication use including dosing and treatment regimens with paracetamol and NSAIDS and application instructions for topical NSAIDS • How to manage adverse effects • When to seek further care and/or treatment.' GENERAL ADVICE: physical interventions that may provide adequate pain relief on their own e.g. hot and cold therapy; other appropriate interventions based on the reported injury e.g. ice, immobilisation and compression therapy; evidence for complementary medicines and fish oil per Therapeutic Guidelines; possible adverse effects and interactions of complementary medicines with conventional medicines. 'The agreed management plan should be shared with members of the patient's multidisciplinary healthcare team, with the patient's consent.' Flowchart: 'Communicate agreed management plan with patient and patient's medical practitioner. Document all aspects of management plan.'

gates.criterion: Advice and counselling provided (possible diagnosis, management options, medicine use incl. dosing and treatment regimens, adverse effects, when to seek further care) and plan communicated with the patient

steps.description: GENERAL ADVICE / CLINICAL REVIEW: 'The patient should be advised to see a medical practitioner if: • The pain relief provided is not adequate; or • Symptoms do not start to improve within 5 days, or • Their pain or other symptoms worsen; or • They experience new pain or symptoms.' 'Clinical review with the pharmacist is generally not required. If the condition does not improve or resolve, the patient should be advised to see a medical practitioner for further investigation.'

gates.criterion: Condition improves or resolves and no escalation trigger (inadequate pain relief, no improvement within 5 days, worsening symptoms, new symptoms) is present

steps.description: CLINICAL DOCUMENTATION AND COMMUNICATION: 'The pharmacist must make an electronic clinical record of the patient consultation, and a record in a pharmacy dispensing system regarding the supply of any medications under this service, in accordance with the Authority.' 'Where a patient has a My Health Record, the pharmacist must ensure the details of the supply are uploaded to My Health Record, unless requested otherwise by the patient.' Key Points: 'Pharmacists must make a full clinical record of the consultation and the details of all consultations and outcomes must be recorded using secure digital software. Records must be stored securely for minimum seven (7) years.' If the patient consents to disclosure, the consultation record 'must be shared within a week following the consultation'.

gates.criterion: Electronic clinical record and pharmacy dispensing system record made for the supply; My Health Record updated unless the patient requests otherwise; records stored securely for minimum seven (7) years

steps.description: Referral destinations when any red flag or referral criterion is met at any gate: 'Patients who meet any of the referral criteria below are not eligible for this service and must be referred to their regular medical practitioner or health service, or in instances of urgent care to the Emergency Department.' Flowchart destinations: 'Refer to GP.' (age under 18, consent not obtained) and 'Refer to Emergency Department or GP.' (red flags/exclusions present). 'Patients who have requested the service but are not eligible should be referred to their regular medical practitioner or health service.'

gates.criterion: Any red flag warning sign or Section G referral criterion met at any point in the pathway

Also referenced in counselling ('dosing and treatment regimens with paracetamol and NSAIDS') and Section J (Therapeutic Guidelines: Principles of paracetamol use for musculoskeletal pain). review_followup.when: If the pain relief provided is not adequate; if symptoms do not start to improve within 5 days; if pain or other symptoms worsen; or if new pain or symptoms are experienced

open_questions.topic: Flowchart gate wording 'acute respiratory signs' in a musculoskeletal practice standard
open_questions.observed: Page 3 flowchart: 'Does the patient have any acute respiratory signs, red flags, or exclusions?'
open_questions.why_unclear: The service is for mild, acute musculoskeletal pain, so 'acute respiratory' appears to be wording carried over from another template. Both readings are recorded: as printed ('acute respiratory signs') and as possibly intended (any acute signs). Not reconciled.

open_questions.topic: No dose, frequency, strength, duration, max dose or quantity-to-supply printed for any Approved Medicine
open_questions.observed: Section A lists only drug names under 'Oral formulations of:'; Section J and NB1 direct pharmacists to Therapeutic Guidelines: Pharmacological management of acute pain and Principles of NSAID use for musculoskeletal pain.
open_questions.why_unclear: The document deliberately defers dosing to external guidelines that were not supplied with this batch; treatment fields are left empty rather than invented.

open_questions.topic: No emergency (000/ambulance) referral category printed
open_questions.observed: Referral destinations printed are 'their regular medical practitioner or health service', 'GP' and 'in instances of urgent care to the Emergency Department'.
open_questions.why_unclear: There is no explicit emergency/ESCALATE_000 category in this document, so referral.emergency is empty. Whether an emergency escalation pathway exists under local policy is unknown.

open_questions.topic: Paracetamol named as management option but not listed as an Approved Medicine
open_questions.observed: H. BACKGROUND (page 6): 'pharmacotherapy (paracetamol and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)) should be considered in the overall management plan'; Section A Approved Medicines (page 2) lists oral NSAIDs only. Section J also references Therapeutic Guidelines: Principles of paracetamol use for musculoskeletal pain.
open_questions.why_unclear: Contradiction between background guidance and the approved supply list is recorded without reconciliation; whether paracetamol may be supplied (vs only recommended) under the Authority is not stated.

open_questions.topic: Topical NSAIDs mentioned in counselling though Section A lists oral formulations only
open_questions.observed: Page 9: 'Product and medication use including dosing and treatment regimens with paracetamol and NSAIDS and application instructions for topical NSAIDS'; Section A (page 2) states 'Oral formulations of:' only.
open_questions.why_unclear: Contradiction recorded without reconciliation: topical NSAID supply does not appear to be within the Approved Medicines list but is referred to in the counselling requirements.

open_questions.topic: Legal basis / the 'Authority' instrument not printed
open_questions.observed: 'Approved Medicines as listed in the NSW Health Authority (dated 25 February 2026)'; 'under the Authority'; approval signature 'Dr Kerry Chant AO PSM ... 25 February 2026'. No regulation name or poisons schedule provision is printed.
open_questions.why_unclear: The enabling instrument is referenced but not reproduced, so legal_basis describes what is printed and flags the gap.

open_questions.topic: Eligibility combinatorics not stated for the inclusion list
open_questions.observed: The flowchart presents sequential Yes/No gates; Section G states patients 'must be aged 18 years and older' plus 'Patients who meet any of the referral criteria below are not eligible'.
open_questions.why_unclear: The document does not explicitly state AND/OR semantics for the inclusion set; defaulted to all_of per the spec, with INC-2 recorded confidence 'unclear'.

open_questions.topic: Referral/exclusion list explicitly not exhaustive
open_questions.observed: 'Note that these are not exhaustive lists.' (page 5) and 'The prompts provided below are not exhaustive, pharmacists should maintain an open mind and be aware of cognitive bias.' (page 6)
open_questions.why_unclear: The document states the lists are incomplete, so the captured exclusion set cannot be treated as complete; clinical judgement catch-all (EXC-2) applies.

open_questions.topic: Duplicate printed referral criterion: intoxication
open_questions.observed: 'The patient is intoxicated due to drugs and/or alcohol.' appears as a bullet at the end of page 5 and again as the final bullet on page 6 within the same referral list.
open_questions.why_unclear: Recorded once as EXC-11/RF-23 with a note; unclear whether the repetition is intentional emphasis or a document editing artefact.

open_questions.topic: Multi-page statements and referral-block provenance
open_questions.observed: EXC-1 sentence starts on page 4 and finishes on page 5; the referral destinations appear on pages 3, 4-5 and 10; the red-flag box and referral criteria sit on pages 5-6.
open_questions.why_unclear: Provenance uses the first page marker under which each statement appears; the full page ranges are recorded here as required by the spec.

open_questions.topic: Table 1 (mechanical versus inflammatory pain) is a two-column table extracted with interleaved lines
open_questions.observed: Page 8 Table 1 columns 'Inflammatory pain' and 'Mechanical pain (musculoskeletal)' are interleaved in the plain-text extraction (e.g. '• Improves with exercise/movement • May worsen with').
open_questions.why_unclear: Column boundaries may be misaligned; each feature is attributed to the column it appears to belong to, and this note flags possible mis-association.

open_questions.topic: Specific contraindications, precautions, interactions and pregnancy/lactation rules not printed
open_questions.observed: Section G (page 5) and Section J (page 9) require pharmacists to 'consult the Therapeutic Guidelines and other relevant references to confirm management is appropriate, including for: Contraindications and precautions / Drug interactions / Pregnancy and lactation'.
open_questions.why_unclear: No drug-specific contraindication list is reproduced in this document, so none could be transcribed; the check exists only as a pathway gate.

open_questions.topic: 'Inadequate response to optimal treatment' - 'optimal treatment' undefined
open_questions.observed: 'There is inadequate response to optimal treatment or pain/other symptoms worsen' (page 6).
open_questions.why_unclear: The document does not define what constitutes optimal treatment, its duration, or how response is measured, so the trigger cannot be made evaluable.

open_questions.topic: No fixed clinical review interval printed
open_questions.observed: 'Clinical review with the pharmacist is generally not required.' (page 10); escalation triggers are symptom-based (e.g. no improvement within 5 days) rather than a scheduled review.
open_questions.why_unclear: No review timeframe is specified, so review_followup entries are all condition-based; whether a local service requires a scheduled review is unknown.

open_questions.topic: Consent record sharing 'within a week' - exact timeframe ambiguous
open_questions.observed: 'If the patient consents to the disclosure, the record must be shared within a week following the consultation' (page 4).
open_questions.why_unclear: 'Within a week' could mean 7 calendar days from consultation; the document does not define business days vs calendar days.

open_questions.topic: Patients aged over 50 years - consideration printed with no escalation action
open_questions.observed: 'For patients aged over 50 years, consider the increased risk of serious underlying pathologies such as malignancy and minimal-trauma fractures.' (page 7)
open_questions.why_unclear: No threshold, action or referral requirement is printed for this consideration (recorded as exclusion exception EXE-1); unclear whether it is a soft prompt or a mandatory check.

open_questions.topic: Pathway gates with on_fail 'unclear'
open_questions.observed: Steps PW-1-S4, PW-1-S5, PW-1-S9, PW-1-S10 (third gate), PW-1-S11 and PW-1-S13 have gates where the document does not state what happens on failure.
open_questions.why_unclear: The flowchart prints failure branches only for the age, red-flag/exclusion and consent gates; later steps' failure handling is not specified, so 'unclear' is recorded rather than inferred.

open_questions.topic: No first-line ranking among Approved Medicines printed
open_questions.observed: Section A lists nine oral medicines alphabetically with no hierarchy; NB1 says NSAID selection should be based on patient factors.
open_questions.why_unclear: No medicine is designated first-line in the document, so all treatments are recorded first_line=false rather than assuming a preference.

open_questions.topic: Pain severity rating scale/tool not specified
open_questions.observed: 'The patient rates their pain as moderate to severe...' (page 5) and 'Pain severity is subjective and should be interpreted in the context of the patient's presentation' (page 7), with no scale (e.g. NRS/VAS) printed.
open_questions.why_unclear: The severity-based inclusion/exclusion cannot be evaluated numerically because no rating instrument or cut-offs are given.

open_questions.topic: Referral block spans pages 3, 4-5 and 10
open_questions.observed: Routine destinations ('Refer to GP.', 'their regular medical practitioner or health service', 'see a medical practitioner') and urgent destination ('Emergency Department') appear across pages 3-5 and 10.
open_questions.why_unclear: One shared provenance object is required for the referral block; page 3 (first appearance) is used and the range is noted here.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Obtain and verify the NSW Health Authority (dated 25 February 2026) - its Approved Medicines list and training requirements are referenced but not reproduced in this document.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The controlling instrument for supply and training is external to the supplied PDF; scope and eligibility depend on its contents.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Dose, frequency, duration, max dose, strength and quantity-to-supply for each Approved Medicine (celecoxib, etoricoxib, indometacin, ketoprofen, meloxicam, naproxen IR/MR, piroxicam, diclofenac) from the relevant Therapeutic Guidelines topics.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: No dosing information is printed in the Practice Standard; a prescribing support module cannot evaluate supply without it.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Whether paracetamol and topical NSAIDs may be supplied or only recommended under the Authority (Section A lists oral formulations only, while Background and counselling sections refer to paracetamol and topical NSAIDs).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Direct contradiction inside the document; affects what the module permits.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Legal basis/exemption under which supply occurs ('the Authority' is referenced but no regulation or poisons schedule provision is named).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Required protocol field; cannot be inferred from the document.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm with NSW Health the intended flowchart wording 'Does the patient have any acute respiratory signs, red flags, or exclusions?' for this musculoskeletal service.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Wording appears to be a template carry-over and gates eligibility; must be clarified before go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Local emergency escalation policy (000 / ambulance / immediate emergency care) - no emergency referral category is printed in this document.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The document routes urgent care to the Emergency Department but never states an emergency/000 action.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Referral destinations and timeframes: what constitutes 'urgent care to the Emergency Department' vs 'Refer to GP', and expected timeframes for each.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Actions differ by destination and urgency; the document gives no timeframe.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Local thresholds for the clinical-judgement catch-all 'refer any patient not considered appropriate for the service for any reason'.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Open-ended exclusion criterion needs local policy to be operable.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Which version of the Therapeutic Guidelines (and Australian Medicines Handbook) is authoritative for contraindications, drug interactions, pregnancy/lactation, NSAID selection and paracetamol use.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The document defers all clinical decision detail to external references that must be pinned for a rules engine.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Verification requirements for 'approved pharmacist' status: general registration check and completion of the training detailed in the Authority.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Practitioner eligibility gate; training provider/curriculum not printed.

hugh_to_confirm.item: My Health Record upload default and consent capture, plus record retention (minimum seven (7) years) and the approved secure digital software.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Documentation obligations mix mandatory rules and patient-choice exceptions; local systems/policy must be confirmed.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Pain severity assessment tool and cut-offs to use for 'mild' vs 'moderate to severe' pain.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Eligibility turns on severity rating but no scale or threshold is printed.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Whether 'Clinical review with the pharmacist is generally not required' conflicts with any local service requirement for scheduled follow-up.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: 'Generally' is hedged language; local service model may require a review interval.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Scope of complementary medicines/fish oil advice under the service ('Evidence for the use of complementary medicines and fish oil as per the Therapeutic Guidelines: Complementary medicines for the management of musculoskeletal pain').
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Advice scope for products outside the Approved Medicines list needs confirmation.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Identification of 'participating approved pharmacist' / 'approved pharmacist' and the approved training modules and education providers.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Service participation criteria are referenced but not enumerated in the document.
